narrative.text: The GRADE approach to rating confidence in an estimate of effect. Rows give study design — randomized controlled trials, which start at high confidence, and observational studies, which start at low. Between them, five reasons for lowering confidence (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias) and three for raising it (large effect, dose response, and plausible confounding that would either reduce a demonstrated effect or suggest a spurious one). The right-hand column gives the four resulting levels — high, moderate, low and very low — each shown with the circle notation, from four filled circles down to one.

basis.saw: a comparison table of four rapid-review types

narrative.text: A comparison of four types of rapid review — a traditional systematic review conducted rapidly, a rapid review of systematic reviews, a rapid review of systematic reviews plus primary studies, and a rapid review of primary studies only — across twelve methodological dimensions. The traditional review allows up to 16 weeks where the three rapid forms allow up to 12. It differs from them throughout: no restrictions on literature search or number of databases against restrictions and 2–3 databases; complete data-extraction verification against one reviewer with selected verification; outcomes restricted to four or fewer against two to four with more if available. Rows also cover question types, number of questions, use of systematic reviews, grey literature, screening, study designs included, risk-of-bias assessment, and assessment of the quality of the body of evidence.
